pumac-2017-number-theory-a-07.prompt: Compute the number of ordered pairs of integers $(a,b)$, where $0\le a<17$ and $0\le b<17$, such that $y^2\equiv x^3+ax+b\pmod{17}$ has an even number of solutions $(x,y)$, where $0\le x<17$ and $0\le y<17$ are integers.
pumac-2017-number-theory-a-07.reviewNote: Official answer 113 = (p^2+3p-1)/3 misses the polynomial x^3 (a = b = 0), whose single (triple) root makes the solution count odd (17 solutions). A brute-force count over all 289 pairs gives 112. Stored 112; the official 113 is also accepted.

pumac-2017-number-theory-a-08.prompt: Find the minimum value attained by $\displaystyle\sum_{m=1}^{100}\gcd(M-m,400)$ for $M$ an integer in the range $[1746,2017]$.
